abstract: Great interest is devoted to electro-optic (EO) polymers since they allow the fabrication of very high performance microwave photonic components, such as optical modulators and analog-to-digital converters, due to a much better velocity matching between microwave and optical signal as well as a higher EO coefficient than the very popular inorganic LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> material. This paper studies the influence of nanoparticle loading on optical properties of EO polymers. We are interested in the host-guest system. A proof of concept is investigated by using a polymer matrix in which we add Disperse Red One (DR1) chromophores. Our first investigations are realized with TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles, which are transparent at the telecommunications wavelength of 1.55 μm. The m-lines technique allows measuring the refractive index of the films. As expected, the refractive index increases when weight-weight percentage of DR1 to PMMA increases from 3.5 wt.% to 14 wt.%. The refractive index increase tends to saturate at high DR1 percentages, which suggests that DR1 aggregation occurs. By adding TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles, a further increase is observed that we discuss by considering both the refractive index of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and the possibility to decrease the DR1 aggregation.

articleTitle: Unified Road Infrastructure Safety System using Visible Light Communication
abstract: Detection of dangerous events and situations is becoming an important direction in the field of road safety, intelligent traffic, and monitoring and control systems. Traditional ways of highlighting and detecting traffic hazards have reached a peak based on intelligent systems. Their detection is done through applications, based on high-resolution video cameras with and without the feedback of LIDAR sensors. The current approach is based on a detection threshold and focuses on the transmission of information from devices that identify danger to intelligent traffic management systems, and other vehicles. By using computer vision the camera feed is analyzed and relevant data is classified to the driver and then transmitted promptly to an intelligent traffic light system capable of changing its status depending on the message received from the installed systems either at the level of road infrastructure or embedded in participant cars. On this approach, we propose a module to enable bidirectional communication with a traffic light through modulation of the available light sources via a microcontroller and a light receiver to enable data transmission and reception to achieve data transmission on the identified objects, type, direction, back and forth to the road infrastructure and other participants. The proposed system takes part in a larger under development safety system that includes several modules dedicated to the automotive safety sector.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of electromagnetic radiation origination from WLAN access point using 802.11a, g, n and ac technologies
abstract: In this paper, an experimental analysis of electromagnetic radiation originating from the WLAN(Wireless Local Area Network) access point using different WLAN technologies (802.11a / g / n / ac) was performed. The measurement results, obtained in the lab topology of the WLAN for data download service, show that the electric field strength significantly depends on the deployed technology, as well as on used frequency band. Measured values indicate that the electric field strength is highest in the case of 802.11n technology in the 5GHz frequency at 5GHz, whereby all obtained values are below the prescribed reference levels.

articleTitle: Computer Vision Aided 2D Motion Sequence Test Supervision
abstract: This study presents an object trajectory tracking system that would increase the reliability and accuracy of motion sequence testing for devices such as accelerometers. By attaching an ArUco marker to the device, we are able to perform pose estimation for the device and calculate the coordinates of the device in a coordinate system of our choosing. By tracking the coordinates in consecutive frames, the trajectory is noted. While testing, speed corrections are displayed. We are able to compare the test trajectory to a reference trajectory and determine whether the test device is malfunctioning, or the motion was performed incorrectly. In case of an incorrect trajectory, the exact section that was incorrectly performed is determined, and rectified in subsequent testing. This eliminates uncertainty between the test device malfunction and incorrect device motion performed during the test, thus providing more accurate test results.

articleTitle: Simulation of all-terminal reliability of an undirected network using the reliability polynomial
abstract: This paper discusses the modeling of terminal network reliability using reliability polynomials. A simulator was developed and its results compared with the values of the reliability polynomial. The lack of exact methods for calculating reliability polynomials is considered and an approximate method for calculating reliability polynomials covering the shortcomings of exact methods is implemented. A comparative performance analysis of the network reliability simulation, an approximate and exact method for determining the reliability polynomial, was performed.
